metadata.title: Vernier: Tunable-Precision Certified Abstract Domains for Floating-Point Programs — VMCAI 2027 Artifact
metadata.description:
Self-contained artifact for the VMCAI 2027 paper Vernier: Tunable-Precision Certified Abstract Domains for Floating-Point Programs. A single Docker image bundles the Rust implementation (certkernel), the Lean 4 mechanization of the certificate checkers, and the Apron/ELINA/VPL baselines; no network or repository access is needed at evaluation time.

It reproduces the paper's claims: (C1) float-speed LP with rational soundness and the tunable (k, ℓ) domain family; (C2) an offline-certified fixpoint 8–29× faster than VPL's fastest working configuration; (C3) independently checkable certificates whose checker soundness is mechanized in Lean 4 (soundness theorems resting only on the standard axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorry); and (C4) two genuine soundness bugs the mechanization exposed. Includes smoke.sh, claim-by-claim reproduction scripts, expected outputs, and a reuse/extension guide.

Targets the Available, Functional, and Reusable badges. Third-party baselines (Apron, ELINA, VPL) are included under their own (LGPL) licenses.

metadata.title: SeedScope Public Reproducibility Release: Seed-Level Reliability, Practical Equivalence, and Cross-Architecture Validation in Dense Object Detection
metadata.description:
SeedScope is a reproducibility release accompanying the manuscript
“SeedScope: A Detector-Agnostic Framework for Seed-Level Reliability,
Practical Equivalence, and Cross-Architecture Validation in Dense Object Detection.”

The release contains canonical seed-level evaluation artifacts for YOLOv8m
and RT-DETR-L, including per-seed metrics, statistical outputs,
cross-architecture summaries, verified RT-DETR-L practical-equivalence
analyses, provenance records, SHA-256 manifests, and portable verification
scripts.

The package supports reproducibility and independent audit of the empirical
results reported in the manuscript. It does not redistribute the SKU-110K
dataset, model checkpoint binaries, superseded historical RT-DETR evidence,
or private computing-environment paths.

The associated manuscript was submitted to IEEE Access.

metadata.title: Reproducibility Package for Wuming Ternary
metadata.description:
This record contains the frozen computational artifact accompanying the publication Wuming Ternary. It preserves the exact WT 1.0.1 core, guarded wire formats, native modules, CUDA and RTL sources, frozen comparator snapshots, public inputs, deterministic generators, preregistrations, sealed results, statistical procedures, evidence indexes, integrity manifests, and executable release verifiers required to inspect and reconstruct the claims reported in the publication.

Reproduction architecture

The package separates correctness, direct performance, unified-mechanism validation, boundary validation, wire conformance, robustness, and nonidentifiability. Stage 1 supplies the frozen correctness and feasibility gate. Stage 2 uses disjoint entities and executes only after every correctness component has passed.

Each formal experiment retains its own source identity, dependency versions, seeds or public-file hashes, comparator contract, primary endpoint, multiplicity rule, confidence procedure, Stage 1 result, Stage 2 result, and verification entry point. Registered predecessor endpoints are preserved wherever a sealed optimization changed the measured hot path while retaining exact output and the comparison contract.

Data and evidence binding

Generated inputs are reconstructed from frozen scripts and seeds. Public-file experiments use fifteen entity-isolated Canterbury, Large, and pi inputs totaling 15,006,053 bytes. Their source locations, revisions, byte sizes, and SHA-256 digests are recorded in the package.

EVIDENCE_INDEX.json maps the manuscript’s tables and endpoints to their underlying evidence. PAPER_NUMBERS.json is the machine source for reported experimental values. PAPER_ASSERTIONS.json records required manuscript claims and version-chain statements. ENVIRONMENT.json records the original formal execution environment.

The package-internal manifest.json binds the final publication PDF to the paper-number, paper-assertion, and evidence-index files. MANIFEST.sha256 records the SHA-256 digest of every tracked package file. The external manifest.json and WT 1.0.0 Hash.txt bind the final publication PDF and the standalone reproduction-package ZIP.

Verification and execution scope

The root verifier checks all tracked package files, frozen inputs, public-source hashes, current and predecessor version identities, reported paper numbers, evidence indexes, privacy-sensitive paths, and internal release links. The release verifier checks the final delivery filenames, external PDF and ZIP hashes, internal evidence binding, DOCX and PDF numerical parity, OfficeMath requirements, fonts, publication metadata, and selected evidence assertions.

Exact round trips, frame bytes, generated inputs, source hashes, code lengths, rejection counts, statistical rules, evidence indexes, and package integrity can be verified deterministically. Timing values remain hardware dependent. GPU endpoints require a compatible NVIDIA GPU and CUDA environment; CPU verification paths remain available without one.

The package excludes unrelated development trials, caches, credentials, private material, and machine-specific absolute paths. WT-authored code, experiment material, evidence indexes, and documentation are licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Third-party software and public corpora remain governed by their original licenses and provenance statements.

Publication concept DOI:
10.5281/zenodo.22084900

Reproduction-package concept DOI:
10.5281/zenodo.22084898

metadata.title: binkma-v/sp-aurora: CoCoDiff SC26 artifact — communication library
metadata.description:
Artifact for the SC26 paper "CoCoDiff: Optimizing Collective Communications for Distributed Diffusion Transformer Inference Under Ulysses Sequence Parallelism" (Bin Ma, Xingjian Ding, Tekin Bicer, Pengfei Su, Dong Li).

This repository is the communication library, sp_aurora. It contains the three mechanisms themselves plus a stand-alone all-to-all micro-benchmark:

  • TAPA — splits each Ulysses all-to-all into an intra-GPU tile-to-tile phase and an inter-GPU phase run as two parallel 6-rank Xe Link rings, matching Aurora's 12x bandwidth hierarchy (185 GB/s intra-GPU, 15 GB/s Xe Link, 25 GB/s Slingshot-11).
  • V-First scheduling — launches V's phase-1 exchange on a background thread so it overlaps Q/K normalization and RoPE.
  • V-Major selective communication — an L1 metric over cached V selects the active token projections; only that subset crosses the inter-GPU links.

The artifact is split across two repositories and both are required. The companion inference engine imports this library at run time.

| | Repository | | --- | --- | | Library | binkma-v/sp-aurora (this one) | | Engine | binkma-v/xDit-intel |

Requires Aurora or another Intel Data Center GPU Max system. See README.md for the build (the SYCL kernels are optional; the package degrades gracefully without them).

Licensed under Apache 2.0. Derives from ring-flash-attention; MIT notices are preserved in NOTICE.

metadata.title: binkma-v/xDit-intel: CoCoDiff SC26 artifact — inference engine
metadata.description:
Artifact for the SC26 paper "CoCoDiff: Optimizing Collective Communications for Distributed Diffusion Transformer Inference Under Ulysses Sequence Parallelism" (Bin Ma, Xingjian Ding, Tekin Bicer, Pengfei Su, Dong Li).

This repository is the inference engine: the xfuser engine extended to drive the four evaluated DiT models through CoCoDiff, together with the per-model latency drivers, inpainting evaluators, PBS job scripts, and figure-generating scripts.

The artifact is split across two repositories and both are required. The engine imports the companion communication library at run time; if that import fails it silently falls back to a flat all-to-all and every configuration measures the same latency.

| | Repository | | --- | --- | | Engine | binkma-v/xDit-intel (this one) | | Library | binkma-v/sp-aurora |

Requires Aurora or another Intel Data Center GPU Max system. See README.md for setup and the environment variables that select the Flat / TAPA / CoCoDiff configurations, and jobs/README.md for the mapping from each figure and table in the paper to the script that produces it.

Licensed under Apache 2.0, inherited from upstream xDiT.

metadata.title: RNArchBench: A Reproducible Benchmark and Replication Suite for React Native Architecture Performance
metadata.description:
RNArchBench is a reproducible benchmark and replication suite for evaluating performance trade-offs between React Native Legacy Architecture, React Native New Architecture, and native Android. The suite provides benchmark applications, canonical empirical datasets, analysis scripts, figures, reproducibility utilities, and documentation for five performance scenarios: update-to-next-frame-callback delay, long-list scrolling, JS-driven and native-driven animations, JavaScript-native communication, and cold-start performance.

Version 1.0.4 establishes a fully consistent SoftwareX artifact: the exact versioned GitHub tag, CFF metadata, manuscript, and Zenodo archive share the same reserved version DOI. It strengthens prospective reproducibility with strict canonical condition-grid validation, Scenario 4 timing boundaries that exclude correctness checks from throughput measurement, a separate full correctness diagnostic, a fully pinned analysis environment, figure-integrity checks, and CI APK builds.

The software was developed as the replication artifact accompanying research on the performance implications of React Native architectural migration.

hits.title: RNArchBench: A Reproducible Benchmark and Replication Suite for React Native Architecture Performance
